final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced on 9.12.0 only. It is already fixed at this revision (6f37b07, 9.15.0).

**Expected:** `no-lonely-if` either skips the report or gives a fix that keeps the outer `else` attached to the outer `if (true)`.

**Actual (9.12.0):** I ran the reporter's exact file through the CLI. It reports `4:9 no-lonely-if`, and `--fix` rewrites line 4 to `else if (false) {}`. After that the trailing `else throw ...` belongs to the inner `if`. Running the code before the fix: no throw. After the fix it throws "This `else` should have been unreachable!".

**On this checkout:** no report and no fix, for both the CLI and `Linter`. The repo's own test file already lists this pattern as valid: `"if (a) if (a) {} else { if (b) {} } else {}"` in `tests/lib/rules/no-lonely-if.js`. That test passes (17/17 in `no-lonely-if.js`). The local history has `9db5b15 fix: unsafe report for no-lonely-if (#19087)`, which touches `lib/rules/no-lonely-if.js` and `lib/rules/utils/ast-utils.js`. I only saw that commit's title in `git log` and didn't open the commit or PR.

**Trigger:** the `else { if … }` block is the alternate of an `if` that is itself the unbraced body of an outer `if`, and that outer `if` has an `else`. Removing the braces moves the outer `else` onto the inner `if`. Likely cause: in 9.12.0 the rule only checked `astUtils.areBracesNecessary(parent, …)`. That function doesn't look at an `else` sitting after the enclosing statement.

**Run:**
```
npm i --no-save --prefix /tmp/eslint-9.12 eslint@9.12.0 && ESLINT_PATH=/tmp/eslint-9.12/node_modules/eslint node repro/no-lonely-if-19033.js
```
This exits 1 with an assertion that the fix changed the program's behaviour. Without `ESLINT_PATH`, the script uses this checkout's `lib/api` and exits 0.

**Artifacts:** `repro/no-lonely-if-19033.js`, a script that lints, fixes and runs the code before and after. It's the only file I added; no production code was changed.
